paper.title: RoboNeuron: A Middle-Layer Infrastructure for Agent-Driven Orchestration in Embodied AI
paper.central_claim: RoboNeuron derives agent-callable tools from robot schemas, unifies direct and persistent PIC execution with explicit lifecycle control, and localizes backend/runtime/preset changes to a stable inference boundary to avoid topology rewiring.

provenance.notes: anchors_version=v2 (3ececdd11cc3d144). Session/receipt unavailable. R04 and main cite this paper: structural match only, not independent rating support. Hash binds taxonomy and cited expectation main. No code run.

sections_read: IV-A-D all Cases I-IV, TableI/Fig3-6 captions

evidence.quote: RoboNeuron is a middleware infrastructure that bridges agent tool calling and robot middleware, rather than a planning algorithm or a replacement for existing robot control stacks.
evidence.support_explanation: Center claim is interface infrastructure, not improved agent planning success.

evidence.quote: The architecture decouples semantics from transport by bifurcating the system into a control plane and a data plane.
evidence.support_explanation: Heterogeneous traffic receives distinct execution/lifecycle treatment.

evidence.quote: The system parses ROS message definitions to resolve fields, including nested structures and arrays, and constructs a structured tool argument schema.
evidence.support_explanation: Schema-derived typed tools target manual wrapper drift.

evidence.quote: A dedicated stop tool manages process cleanup, utilizing a bounded wait period before resorting to a forced termination
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit lifecycle semantics; no measured cleanup reliability/race behavior.

evidence.quote: a 6-DoF end-effector delta in position and orientation together with a gripper command.
evidence.support_explanation: Stable semantic action contract; transport vector alone is not arbitrary compatibility.

evidence.quote: the agent can restart the inference module with the new configuration while the perception and control modules continue to run
evidence.support_explanation: Topology-preserving swap, not live same-process instantaneous replacement.

evidence.quote: Each suite contains 10 tasks, and each task is evaluated over 50 episodes.
evidence.support_explanation: LIBERO denominators present for policy-preservation experiment.
Aggressive preset loses success despite stable I/O; no free performance invariance.
Moderate pruning not uniformly neutral; protocol+pruning combined relative to baseline.

evidence.quote: The real-robot study emphasizes feasibility and runtime semantics rather than large-scale statistical performance.
evidence.support_explanation: No physical task denominators, orchestration success rates or reliability measurement.

evidence.quote: Our current prototype also focuses on topic-based capability exposure and a vector action transport format.
evidence.support_explanation: Services/actions and broader interface generality not evaluated.

evidence.quote: Figure 6 reports latency and normalized speedup on an RTX 4090.
evidence.support_explanation: Inference-side latency evaluated separately from task success; no whole-pipeline cost accounting.

evidence.quote: implementations such as ROS2mcpserver [ 23 ] and ROS2mcp [ 24 ] show that ROS capabilities can be connected to such interfaces in practice.
evidence.support_explanation: Nearest bridging systems described but originals/version-specific comparison absent.

gap.author_gap: Ad-hoc agent/robot wrappers drift, lack composable runtime/lifecycle and require repeated VLA serving re-integration.
gap.checked_gap: Plausible concrete integration defect; cases show fixed interface reuse but do not quantify maintenance savings or orchestration reliability.

claims.text: Schema-derived tools and direct/PIC lifecycle unify orchestration.
claims.setting: Sim multi-platform bases and arm; physical FR3 VLA grasp case.
claims.baseline_control: Mechanism demonstrations, no manual-wrapper or competing MCP deployment trial.
claims.selection_vs_test: Cases appear part of construction validation, no new-schema holdout.
claims.result_denominator: Qualitative cases only; no integration task count/restart failure rate.
counterevidence: No quantitative burden/reliability metric; scope limited to topics.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author describes and illustrates a reconstructible runtime design, not proven broad orchestration reliability.

claims.text: Fixed inference boundary supports backend/preset changes without rewiring.
claims.setting: LIBERO suites and independent OpenVLA 4090 single-step latency.
claims.baseline_control: OpenVLA-OFT versus RN+pruning; OpenVLA runtime overhead variants in figure.
claims.selection_vs_test: Preset comparisons, no held-out migration selection protocol.
claims.result_denominator: 10tasks×50episodes per suite; P50 Spatial99.2,Object98.4,Goal96.8,Long94.4 at1.17x; P75Object89.8/Long89.2.
counterevidence: Backend/preset changes do not guarantee preserved competence; latency study separate from SR model.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Fixed I/O accommodates tested configurations; moderate pruning has mixed small losses, aggressive pruning larger losses.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported LIBERO closed-loop evaluation and mechanism cases support feasibility of a stable schema/PIC inference boundary for tested configurations; neither agent-level success, real counted transfer nor quantified integration-cost reduction is established.
unresolved: No named evaluated LLM agent or counted autonomy orchestration trials.
No claim of improving VLA intelligence or planning should be inferred.

G.reason: Interface drift, long-running lifecycle and backend boundary are concrete engineering problems with ROS2/MCP predecessor discussion; switching/maintenance burden not empirically quantified.

M.reason: Schema derivation and separate control/data plus stable action contract directly address API alignment and replacement. Cross-backend semantics/constraints cannot be guaranteed merely by vector transport.

X.reason: Algorithms1-2 and typed validation/process lifecycle/PIC contract are reconstructible; current topic-only scope and no stress/failure test limit confidence.

measurement.reason: LIBERO task rates have 50-per-task denominators; center infrastructure reliability/reintegration-effort measured only through mechanism cases, and real orchestration/grasp success uncounted (v2 partial denominator anchor).

causality.reason: Fixed surrounding contract supports inference-presets comparison; no direct schema/manual-wrapper or lifecycle ablation, and RN/pruning combination does not isolate middleware success cost.

holdout.reason: Multiple demonstrations/platforms and four familiar benchmark suites, no construction-unused schemas/hardware or controlled held-out backend migration.

statistics.reason: Many LIBERO episodes but no run-to-run variance, failure/restart audit or real trial denominator; not a fully unsupported stat axis.

cost.reason: Pruning speedup and hardware-specific per-step latency are relevant but missing full orchestration/API/development/latency overhead and uncertainty.

reason: B-class reusable harness infrastructure; static system_method, not evaluation benchmark contribution or pure VLA.
